newsitem.title: USA: PJM says record Mid-Atlantic power demand Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: PJM says record Mid-Atlantic power demand Tuesday.

text.p: The operator of the power grid in U.S. Mid-Atlantic states said that record electricity demand was seen on its system Tuesday as hot, humid weather continued to smother the region.

"Today at 5 P.M. (1700 EDT), the PJM Interconnection announced that the electrical load 49,820 megawatts (MW) in the Mid-Atlantic region exceeded the previous all-time peak of 48,524 megawatts set on August 2, 1995," the regional grid operator said in a statment.

The new peak places PJM, officially called the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland Interconnect Pool, as the third largest centrally dispatched entity in the world, moving ahead of the National Grid in England by 1,000 MWs.
The PJM control center coordinates the operation of 540 generators.

Earlier, PJM cautioned that its previous peak load may be exceeded and Monday issued a "hot weather alert" for today, requesting that member utilities in the grid ask customers to conserve energy during hours of peak demand.
A spokesman said electricity demand in the region should remain high Wednesday but PJM had extended the alert for tomorrow.
